source: hand-authored fixture for issues #237/#259 — not shipped data
description: Two entries sharing ONE id and publishing NO substanceName, which is the shape DrugReferenceInjector.matchingEntries groups on its documented getId() fallback. The curated parser drops an entry only for a blank id or name and no DrugReferenceValidity rule reports a duplicate id, so an operator-editable file reaches this. They are one CITABLE entity and NOT a declared substance, so neither the row-attribution clause nor the other-rows dosing section may speak: 'filed separately for the same substance' and 'other rows of this substance' would each claim something this file never said. Both rows publish a band and the bands DIFFER (400 against 200), so both features would have content but for their guards, and they differ in name so a clause would have two names to contrast. The second row carries the alias `tmp-paediatric`, which the first does NOT, and that alias is what puts BOTH rows in one group: the ranked accessors resolve one row per name, so with `trimethoprim` as the only alias the question leg and the order leg both resolved the unqualified row, the group was a single row, interactionSubject short-circuited on it, and BOTH guards were unreachable — every assertion here passed on a group that could not have reached them. Drive the order by `tmp-paediatric` (as both test files do) so the question leg resolves the unqualified row, the order leg resolves this one, and the shared id really does put two rows in one group.
